statement.summary: Corollary 8.2 is split into eight frozen Props, conjoined in `insolvStatement`: the general unsolvability claim (for equivariant maps, `insolvGeneralStatement`, and for offset CA, `insolvGeneralCAStatement`), the two justifications inside the corollary (constants are symmetric; no trajectory leaves S), the leader-election claims (targets asymmetric, never reached, the task unsolvable) and the closing sentence's mathematical core (`leaderRestrictStatement`: an equivariant solver must avoid every symmetric input). The paper does not define 'task' or 'solvable'; Lean introduces `Task`, `Solves`, `RequiresLeavingS`, `leaderTask`, `leaderTaskOn` for this. The paper has no proof environment; `insolv_proved` certifies the frozen type. Since 2026-10-27 the symmetry-breaking sentence (added in v5, reworded in v7) is frozen in the group-07 supplement `S07_Dynamics_SymmetryBreaking.lean`: `insolvSymBreakStatement`, with the hypothesis `RequiresSymmetryBreaking` (on some admissible input every acceptable output breaks a symmetry of it), and `insolvFullStatement` = `insolvStatement` ∧ `insolvSymBreakStatement`.
deltas: The paper does not define 'task': a `Task` is a set of admissible inputs plus, for each input, a set of acceptable outputs (the most general input/output specification).

'Solvable' = `Solves`: from every admissible input the trajectory reaches an acceptable output at SOME step k ≥ 0 (no halting, no stay requirement) — the weakest success notion, so its negation is the strongest unsolvability.
'Requiring, on some input, an output outside S reachable from an input inside S' = `RequiresLeavingS`: some admissible input x ∈ S ALL of whose acceptable outputs lie outside S.
'Translation-equivariant CA' = any map with `Equivariant Φ` (general form), and separately the offset CA `caMap offs φ` of Definition 2.4 (any b, including b = 0).
N > 1 is written `1 < n ^ d`; σ ≥ 2 and N > 1 are kept as stated but are not used by the implications (they make the situation non-degenerate).
'Unique distinguished cell' = some state occupies exactly one cell (the leader state is not fixed in advance).
Leader election (as a task) = all inputs admissible, acceptable outputs = exactly one cell in the leader state ℓ, others arbitrary.

The closing sentence is formalized in its contrapositive: an equivariant (uniform, deterministic, synchronous) solver of leader election on inputs X must have X ∩ S = ∅ — the paper's own example ('restrict ... to asymmetric configurations'), a disclosed strengthening of the literal 'restrict the admissible inputs'.

'Every pattern-recognition or image-processing task whose required output breaks a symmetry of some admissible input' = `RequiresSymmetryBreaking` for EVERY task (the informal task names are not formalized: a generalization). 'Breaks a symmetry' = some translation fixing the input does not fix the output (¬ stab x ≤ stab y), the largest true reading; it is strictly more than `RequiresLeavingS`.

maps.label: symmetric-to-asymmetric tasks are unsolvable

tex.text: Any task requiring, on some input, an output configuration outside $S_{n^d}$ reachable from an input inside $S_{n^d}$ is unsolvable by translation-equivariant CA on $\ZZ_n^d$

lean.text:
∀ T : Task n d σ, RequiresLeavingS T →
      ∀ Φ : Config n d (Fin σ) → Config n d (Fin σ), Equivariant Φ →
        ¬ Solves Φ T

maps.note: The general claim, with 'task', 'requiring' and 'solvable' made precise by the three definitions below.

maps.label: task

lean.text: admissible : Set (Config n d (Fin σ))
accept : Config n d (Fin σ) → Set (Config n d (Fin σ))

maps.note: Not defined in the paper; modelled as admissible inputs + acceptable outputs per input.

maps.label: requires leaving S on some input in S

tex.text: requiring, on some input, an output configuration outside $S_{n^d}$ reachable from an input inside $S_{n^d}$

lean.text: ∃ x ∈ T.admissible, x ∈ SS n d σ ∧ T.accept x ⊆ (SS n d σ)ᶜ

maps.note: One admissible symmetric input whose every acceptable output is asymmetric. If some acceptable output were symmetric the task would not 'require' leaving S.

maps.label: unsolvable

lean.text: ¬ Solves Φ T
∀ x ∈ T.admissible, ∃ k : ℕ, Φ^[k] x ∈ T.accept x

maps.note: Solving = reaching an acceptable output at some time step of the synchronous trajectory; the weakest notion, hence the strongest unsolvability.

maps.label: translation-equivariant CA on ℤ_n^d

lean.text:
Equivariant Φ →
        ¬ Solves Φ T

∀ (b : ℕ) (offs : Fin b → Lat n d) (φ : (Fin b → Fin σ) → Fin σ),
        ¬ Solves (caMap offs φ) T

maps.note: Frozen twice: for every equivariant map, and for the literal offset CA of Definition 2.4.

maps.label: offset CA Φ(s)(u) = φ(s(u+o_1),…,s(u+o_b))

lean.text: fun s u => φ (fun i => s (u + offs i))

maps.note: The global map of Definition 2.4; `caMap_equivariant` proves it is equivariant.

maps.label: σ ≥ 2 and N > 1
maps.note: Kept as stated (N = n^d). Neither is used by the implication: N > 1 makes S nonempty, σ ≥ 2 makes asymmetric outputs exist.

maps.label: standing hypotheses n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1
maps.note: From Definition 2.1 (they already imply N > 1).

maps.label: symmetric inputs exist (all constants lie in S)

tex.text: symmetric inputs exist (all constants lie in $S_{n^d}$)

lean.text:
(∃ x : Config n d (Fin σ), x ∈ SS n d σ) ∧
      ∀ a : Fin σ, (fun _ : Lat n d => a) ∈ SS n d σ

maps.note: Both halves of the parenthetical justification.

maps.label: symmetric inputs exist

lean.text: ∃ x : Config n d (Fin σ), x ∈ SS n d σ

maps.note: S_{n^d} is nonempty.

maps.label: all constants lie in S

lean.text: ∀ a : Fin σ, (fun _ : Lat n d => a) ∈ SS n d σ

maps.note: Every constant configuration is fixed by every translation, in particular by a nonzero one.

maps.label: no trajectory leaves S

lean.text: ∀ s ∈ SS n d σ, ∀ k : ℕ, Φ^[k] s ∈ SS n d σ

maps.note: Trajectory = the iterates Φ^[k] s; the paper derives it from Theorem 8.1 (the certificate uses `isShiftSymmetric_iterate`).

maps.label: this covers leader election

lean.text: ¬ Solves Φ (leaderTask n d σ ℓ)
accept := fun _ => {t | ∃! u : Lat n d, t u = ℓ}

maps.note: Leader election as a task: all inputs admissible, outputs with exactly one cell in state ℓ; unsolvable for every ℓ and every equivariant Φ.

maps.label: unique-distinguished-cell targets are asymmetric

tex.text: the target configuration with a unique distinguished cell is asymmetric for $N>1$

lean.text: HasUniqueDistinguishedCell t → t ∉ SS n d σ

maps.note: Every configuration in which some state occupies exactly one cell lies outside S (the hypothesis N > 1 is kept but not needed).

maps.label: unique distinguished cell

lean.text: ∃ a : Fin σ, ∃! u : Lat n d, t u = a

maps.note: 'Distinguished' = carrying a state no other cell carries; the state is existentially quantified (largest class of targets).

maps.label: leader targets are never reached from symmetric inputs

lean.text: ∀ x ∈ SS n d σ, ∀ k : ℕ, ¬ HasUniqueDistinguishedCell (Φ^[k] x)

maps.note: An intermediate conjunct combining 'symmetric inputs exist', 'no trajectory leaves S' and 'targets asymmetric' — what 'This covers leader election' asserts, frozen separately.

maps.label: leader-election algorithms must break a hypothesis or restrict inputs

tex.text: therefore necessarily break one of the hypotheses (uniformity, determinism, synchrony) or restrict the admissible inputs, e.g.\ to asymmetric configurations

lean.text:
∀ Φ : Config n d (Fin σ) → Config n d (Fin σ), Equivariant Φ →
        Solves Φ (leaderTaskOn n d σ ℓ X) → X ∩ SS n d σ = ∅

maps.note: Contrapositive form: a solver keeping all three hypotheses (= an equivariant global map iterated synchronously) solves leader election on X only if X contains no symmetric input. Stronger than the literal 'restrict' (X ≠ univ).

maps.label: uniformity, determinism, synchrony

lean.text: Equivariant Φ →
Φ^[k] x

maps.note: Uniform local rule with translation-invariant neighbourhood = `Equivariant Φ`; determinism and synchrony = iteration of one global map.

maps.label: restrict the admissible inputs (to asymmetric ones)

tex.text: restrict the admissible inputs, e.g.\ to asymmetric configurations

lean.text: X ∩ SS n d σ = ∅
admissible := X

maps.note: The admissible set X is a parameter of the task; the conclusion says X avoids S entirely.

maps.note: The reference to the specific algorithms of Nichitiu 1999 / Stratmann 2002 is not mathematical; their content is covered by the 'restrict' map for every algorithm.

every pattern-recognition or image-processing
task whose required output breaks a symmetry of some admissible input is
unsolvable

maps.note: Frozen in the supplement of 2026-10-27, for every task (the task names 'pattern-recognition or image-processing' are informal, so the Lean statement covers more). Strictly more than `insolvGeneralStatement`: on Z_4, 0000 → 0101 breaks a symmetry of the input although 0101 is shift-symmetric (`stripeTask_requiresSymmetryBreaking_not_requiresLeavingS`).

maps.label: required output breaks a symmetry of some admissible input

tex.text: whose required output breaks a symmetry of some admissible input

maps.note: Some admissible x such that every acceptable output y lacks a translation fixing x (¬ stab x ≤ stab y); the broken translation may depend on y. The notion of [2019] (p. 2: 'a source configuration has a symmetry not contained in the target').

tex.text:
since $\Stab$ can only grow along a trajectory
(Theorem~\ref{thm:irrev})

maps.note: The stabilizer form of Theorem 8.1, Stab(s) ≤ Stab(Φ s); iterated along the trajectory it gives the clause (proof of `insolvSymBreak_proved`).

maps.label: Corollary 8.2, all mathematical parts

tex.text: Let $\sigma\ge2$ and $N>1$. Any task requiring, on some input, an output configuration outside $S_{n^d}$ reachable from an input inside $S_{n^d}$ is unsolvable by translation-equivariant CA on $\ZZ_n^d$. Indeed, symmetric inputs exist (all constants lie in $S_{n^d}$), and by Theorem~\ref{thm:irrev} no trajectory leaves $S_{n^d}$.
